issues.failure_explanation: Take the trial velocity and pressure in b_Gamma to be zero and take the test velocity v_f^S=0 while v_r^P and w_s^P have a nonzero common normal flux on Sigma. The left side is then 0, whereas the displayed right side is a positive multiple of sum_E h_E^{-1}||flux||_{0,E}^2. Thus the asserted lower bound is false; inverse-face penalty control is supplied by c_Gamma, not by b_Gamma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove b_Gamma from the inverse-face penalty control; bound the b_Gamma consistency terms by delta||v_f||_1^2 + delta^{-1}||flux||_{0,Sigma}^2 via trace/Young and obtain the sum_E h_E^{-1}||flux||^2 term only from c_Gamma, then recheck the gamma and epsilon conditions.
issues.overall_effect: Ellipticity of the A block is unproved, so the kernel/invertibility lemmas and all later semi-discrete and fully discrete well-posedness, stability, and error statements that invoke this coercivity are unsupported as written.
issues.title: False coercivity estimate for the consistency form b_Gamma
issues.why_classification: The displayed inequality is false and the proof cannot stand, but a standard Nitsche penalty-versus-consistency estimate using the already introduced c_Gamma and trace inequalities should recover ellipticity without abandoning the method or its rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, the scaled matrix is nonsingular, and so is the matrix in \eqref{mixed-primal}.

issues.failure_explanation: Backward Euler solves with (1/tau)M+N, equivalently M+tau N after multiplication by tau. Nonsingularity of M+N is only one value of the associated pencil and does not exclude a generalized eigenvalue that makes M+tau N singular. The stated smallness hypothesis is also on the unknown current iterate and is not the small-data condition used to place the linearization in K_h.

failure_location.quote: This resulting matrix has the same structure as \mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}, which is shown to be nonsingular in the proof of Lemma~\ref{invertibilty}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove nonsingularity of M+tau N directly from the saddle-point/DAE structure, with the convective perturbation controlled at the previous time level and propagated by induction, rather than citing invertibility of M+N.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised unique solvability of the fully discrete algebraic system is not established; conditional stability and error estimates for that system lose their well-posedness foundation.
issues.title: Fully discrete uniqueness proof does not follow from invertibility of M+N
issues.why_classification: The result is not necessarily false, but the one-line scaling argument and self-referential hypothesis must be replaced by a contained generalized-eigenvalue/invertibility argument; this does not by itself force a worse rate or a different method.

issues.failure_explanation: The mass matrix has a zero column for p_h^S and no-zero-rows does not exclude algebraic constraints, so consistency of the initial data is not implied. The proof then sets discrete initial values equal to continuous data not shown to belong to the discrete spaces. In the uniqueness part the decisive integrated estimate is placed inside a comment environment, and the convective term for the difference is written as zero although it is only controlled through the K_h smallness assumption.

failure_location.quote: The matrix \(E\) has no zero rows, which implies that the system has no algebraic constraints.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use discrete interpolants/projections for the initial data, verify the discrete DAE consistency constraints, reinstate the integrated energy estimate outside the comment environment, and absorb c(w,tilde u,tilde u) by the K_h smallness rather than setting it to zero.
issues.overall_effect: Existence and uniqueness for the linearized semi-discrete problem, hence well-definedness of the fixed-point operator used in the Nitsche well-posedness theorem, are not proved as written.
issues.title: Semi-discrete DAE existence and uniqueness proof has unsupported consistency and a missing energy step
issues.why_classification: These are real gaps in a central proof, but the needed repairs are local: compatible discrete initial data, a reinstatement of the commented energy computation, and the already available fixed-point smallness estimate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By substituting the bounds for \mathcal{J}_1--\mathcal{J}_9 into~\eqref{ne1} and choosing \epsilon_1 sufficiently small, we obtain the desired bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof does not derive the stated bounds: J_1 through J_8 are only said to be analogous to another paper, the porous-velocity projection Pi_{r,h} is fixed only by its divergence, the theorem uses undefined initial interpolants Q_{r,h}, I_{r,h}, I_{s,h}, and the convection expansion omits the quadratic difference term -e^{n-1}.nabla e^n. The displayed convergence estimate is therefore not established by the proof.

failure_location.quote: the terms \mathcal{J}_1 through \mathcal{J}_8 are estimated analogously, following the approach presented in~\cite{bansal2024lagrange}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must define Pi_{r,h} and all initial interpolants as proper projections, derive explicit bounds for J_1 through J_9 including the quadratic convection difference, and complete the discrete Gronwall argument to the stated norms.
issues.overall_effect: The main advertised a priori error estimate for the fully discrete Nitsche scheme is unsupported; the numerical convergence claims are left without a proved rate in this paper.
issues.title: A priori fully discrete error proof is not carried out and uses an underdefined projection
issues.why_classification: The central error theorem is reduced to an analogy with a different formulation and several undefined or omitted estimates; supplying a complete proof requires a new, substantial error analysis rather than a local correction.
